# Volume 1 — CHAPTER VI. Thirza Makes Up Her Mind

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

ARRIVE there they certainly managed to, nevertheless, when the time came. Mrs. Tranter resided within a large yellow dwelling located at Pale Sands Cove, and she approached the entrance with astonishment and hospitality combined upon her kindly countenance.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0000 }

“Dear, dear,” she cried out, “you happen to be the final people I anticipated seeing today, yet I am truly happy you are here. Will you stable your horse? And how have you been, Nell?”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0001 }

“With no smile, Nell replied, “Thank you, I am doing as fine as could be anticipated.” It appeared that a dark shadow had fallen over her.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0002 }

“I guess we will remain a short time so the mare can rest,” Thirza said, “however, I gave Obed my word that I would return home at an early hour. Truthfully, Mrs. Tranter, an odd error has occurred somewhere, and my purpose in coming here is to locate it. We communicated, Obed and I, requesting that you deliver a boy from the asylum to us. We instructed your brother Robert to inform you that our desire was a boy aged ten or eleven.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0003 }

“Thirza Abernethy, it can’t be!” exclaimed a troubled Mrs. Tranter. “Listen, Robert dispatched a message through his girl Nancy, and didn't she mention that a girl was needed by you—wasn't that it, Flora Odette?” she asked, turning to her daughter who had stepped onto the porch.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0004 }

“Miss Abernethy, she most certainly did,” Flora Odette verified with great sincerity.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0005 }

“I am so very sorry,” Mrs. Tranter remarked. “This is most unfortunate; however, it was definitely not my doing, Miss Abernethy, as you must realize. Having done everything in my power, I believed that I was acting according to your directions. A more dreadfully light-headed girl than Nancy would be hard to find. On numerous occasions, her lack of thought has forced me to give her a thorough tongue-lashing.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0006 }

“We have only ourselves to blame,” Thirza remarked with acceptance. “Rather than entrusting a critical communication to be relayed verbally like that, we ought to have visited you in person. Regardless, since the error occurred, our sole option at present is to correct it. Is it possible for us to return the youngster to the orphanage? They will accept her return, I assume, will they not?”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0007 }

“I guess that’s true,” Mrs. Tranter remarked reflectively, “however, returning her shouldn't be required in my opinion. Yesterday, when Mrs. Peter Scobie came by, she mentioned how she regretted not asking me to bring back a young girl to assist her. As you are aware, Mrs. Peter has many children, making assistance difficult for her to find. Nell is going to be ideal for her needs. It seems to me entirely fortunate.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0008 }

Thirza’s appearance suggested she doubted Providence played a significant role in the affair. A surprisingly favorable opportunity to rid herself of this undesirable orphan had presented itself, yet she failed to experience any gratitude regarding it.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0009 }

Mrs. Peter Scobie was known to her merely by sight as a tiny woman with a shrewish face and not a single bit of extra flesh on her frame. Nevertheless, rumors about her had reached her ears. Mrs. Peter was reputed to be “A terrible worker and driver,” while former servant girls related terrifying stories regarding her disposition, her meanness, and her brood of insolent, argumentative youngsters. The idea of surrendering Nell to her gentle care caused Thirza to experience a pang of guilt.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0010 }

“Well, I’ll enter so that we may discuss the issue,” she stated.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0011 }

“And if Mrs. Peter isn’t walking up the lane this very moment!” Mrs. Tranter cried out, hurriedly ushering her guests through the hall and into the parlor, where a severe coldness hit them as though the air had been filtered through dark green, tightly pulled blinds for such a long time that it was devoid of any warmth it had once held. “That is truly fortunate, because we can resolve the issue immediately. Sit in the armchair, Miss Abernethy. Nell, sit on the ottoman right here and stop wriggling. Let me gather your hats. Flora Odette, head outside and set the kettle on the stove. Good afternoon, Mrs. Scobie. We were only just remarking on how lucky it was that you came by. Allow me to present you two ladies to each other. Mrs. Scobie, Miss Abernethy. Kindly pardon me for a brief second. I neglected to instruct Flora Odette to remove the buns from the oven.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0012 }

Mrs. Tranter hurried off, having raised the blinds first. Nell, who sat silently upon the ottoman with her hands squeezed together in her lap, gazed at Mrs. Scobie as if spellbound. Would she be handed over to the care of this woman with the keen face and keen eyes? She sensed a lump rising in her throat, and a sharp sting affected her eyes. She was starting to fear that she would be unable to hold her tears in check when Mrs. Tranter came back, red-faced and smiling, fully equipped to weigh every single problem—be it physical, mental, or spiritual—and resolve it on the spot.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0013 }

“It appears a error occurred regarding this young girl, Mrs. Scobie,” she stated. “I believed that Mr. and Miss Abernethy were looking to adopt a young girl. That was definitely what I was informed. However, it appears a boy was what they desired. Therefore, if your intentions remain unchanged from yesterday, I believe she will suit you perfectly.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0014 }

Mrs. Scobie quickly scanned Nell’s entire length, moving her eyes from top to bottom.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0015 }

“What is your name, and how many years old are you?” she asked.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0016 }

“Nell Harcourt,” stammered the cowering child, lacking the courage to specify how it should be spelled, “and my age is eleven years.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0017 }

“Humph! You appear to lack substance. However, you possess toughness. It may well be that those with toughness prove superior in the end. Now, should I accept you, it will be necessary for you to be a proper young lady—well-behaved, clever, and polite. You will be required to work for your room and board, without any doubt. Indeed, it seems reasonable for me to relieve you of her, Miss Abernethy. That infant is extremely difficult, and caring for him has left me entirely exhausted. Should it suit you, she can come back to my house with me this very minute.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0018 }

Upon seeing the young girl's drained countenance and its expression of silent despair—the agony of an undefended small being that is trapped again in the snare it had fled—Thirza’s demeanor relaxed as she gazed at Nell. A troubling certainty came over Thirza that failing to answer the plea in that expression would cause it to torment her until her death. Additionally, she was not fond of Mrs. Scobie. Relinquishing a delicate, “highstrung” youth to a person like her! Indeed, taking on the accountability of performing such an action was impossible for her!
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0019 }

“Indeed, I am uncertain,” she uttered deliberately. “It was not my statement that Obed and I were utterly resolved against retaining her. On the contrary, I might mention that Obed leans toward retaining her. My sole reason for coming was to learn the manner in which the error happened. My opinion is that I ought to carry her back home now and discuss the matter further with Obed. Deciding on anything without conferring with him feels wrong to me. Should we come to the conclusion that we will not retain her, our plan is to deliver or convey her to your house tomorrow evening. Should we fail to do so, you can understand therefrom that her permanent home will be with us. Would such an arrangement be satisfactory to you, Mrs. Scobie?”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0020 }

“I guess that must do,” Mrs. Scobie uttered ungraciously.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0021 }

As Thirza spoke, a sunrise began to break across Nell’s face. Initially, the expression of hopeless misery washed away; subsequently, a subtle glow of hope appeared; her eyes became intense and luminous like stars at dawn. The girl appeared utterly transformed; then, shortly after, as Mrs. Tranter and Mrs. Scobie exited to search for a recipe that Mrs. Scobie had arrived to request, she leaped to her feet and darted across the room toward Thirza.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0022 }

“Oh, Miss Abernethy, did you truly state that maybe you would allow me to remain at Grey Shutters?” she asked, using a quiet, raspy breath, as though talking in a normal voice could ruin the wonderful chance. “Did you truly state it? Or was it just my imagination that you did?”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0023 }

“Nell, you really ought to get a handle on your imagination if discerning reality from fantasy is beyond you,” Thirza remarked irritably. “Indeed, those exact words were what I said, and nothing further. Nothing has been finalized, and it may be that we decide to allow Mrs. Scobie to have you in the end. Her need for you is surely far greater than mine.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0024 }

“I’d prefer returning to the asylum over living with her,” Nell exclaimed passionately. “She appears just like a—like a gimlet.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0025 }

Thirza hid a grin, believing that Nell needed to be scolded for making that remark.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0026 }

“It is shameful for a small girl such as you to speak in that manner regarding a lady and a visitor,” she remarked sternly. “Return to your place, sit in silence, keep quiet, and conduct yourself as a well-behaved girl ought to.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0027 }

“I will attempt to perform and become whatever you desire of me, provided you just retain me,” Nell remarked, going back submissively to her ottoman.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0028 }

As they returned to Grey Shutters that evening, Obed was waiting in the lane. Having spotted him pacing there from a distance, Thirza had divined his intent. The sense of comfort evident on his features upon realizing she had successfully brought Nell home was something she was ready for. Nevertheless, she refrained from discussing the matter with him until the two of them were in the yard behind the barn, engaged in milking the cows. It was at that moment that she concisely recounted Nell’s past to him and conveyed what had transpired during her meeting with Mrs. Tranter.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0029 }

“That Scobie woman wouldn't be given a dog I had any affection for,” Obed stated with an uncharacteristic burst of energy.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0030 }

“Her way doesn’t really suit my taste,” Thirza confessed, “yet the alternative is us retaining her, Obed. And, because you appear to desire her, I guess I am agreeable—or forced to be. I have pondered the concept so long that I am somewhat accustomed to it. A duty of sorts is what it feels like. Raising a child, a girl in particular, is something I have never done, and I suppose I will fail miserably at it. Even so, my best effort will be given. As for my part, Obed, she is permitted to remain.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0031 }

A radiance of pleasure lit up the timid countenance of Obed.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0032 }

“Ah, I figured you would end up viewing it that way, Thirza,” said he. “Such an intriguing little creature she is.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0033 }

“It’d be more useful if you could describe her as a helpful little thing,” Thirza replied, “but I’ll ensure it becomes my task to train her to be just that. And remember, Obed, you must not interfere with my ways. Maybe an old maid isn’t very knowledgeable about raising a youngster, but I suppose she understands more than an old bachelor. Therefore, you simply let me handle her. When I prove unsuccessful, that will be soon enough for you to meddle.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0034 }

“There, there, Thirza, you may do as you wish,” Obed offered comfortingly. “Just treat her with as much goodness and kindness as you are able to while avoiding spoiling her. I have a feeling she belongs to the type that allows you to accomplish anything with them, provided you first win their affection.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0035 }

Thirza gave a sniff to convey her disdain for the views Obed held regarding anything connected to women, after which she headed toward the dairy carrying the pails.
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0036 }

“I won’t inform her this evening that she is permitted to remain,” she thought to herself, while pouring the milk through the strainer into the creamers. “Her excitement would be so great that she would not catch a single wink of sleep. Thirza Abernethy, you are truly committed now. Could you ever have imagined a time when you would be taking in an orphan girl? That is astonishing in itself; yet it is even more astonishing that Obed is the one responsible for it, considering how he always appeared to possess such a deep-seated fear of little girls. Regardless, the trial has been agreed upon, and heaven alone can tell what the outcome will be.”
{: #nw-v01-c06-p0037 }
